notes.body:
Four rulings the game did not follow yet:
- **A Summon pushed, pulled or swapped onto your Step Trap sets it off** (the forced-movement ruling). Sliding over one still does not, and Gallows Step and the other "moves onto" Traps still want the Summon's own move.
- **Mordrec's Gabl is a true replacement:** a Summon he sends into the Void instead of the graveyard fires no Demise. He asks at the death, before anything resolves.
- **Crystal Bastion is one of the protectors you pick from:** a Shockwave asks which protector takes it (Bastion or Summon) on a Summon or a Building. With no pick, the one nearest death takes it.
- **Goad adds up:** a printed Goad plus Bountyleaf Ranger's granted Goad is +2. Before, the printed one hid the grant. Two Rangers give Goad 2.
- **The rules codex** now carries the five forced-movement rulings of 2026-09-29 (rules-core.md, Movement).

The designer's rulings on the website's open points:
- **A kill resolves inside combat, Onslaught after it.** When one attack kills, its Dominate and the victim's Demise now resolve before the attacker's Onslaught.
- **Elusive answers any ability that targets its Summon** - an enemy Manifest, Infiltrate or Agility included, not only Spells and activated abilities.
- **Nothing is immune to Poison:** the last of the old Mechanical exception is gone from Venomous and Contagious.
- **In-game reminders corrected:** Chill ("deactivates and depletes; a target already deactivated becomes Frozen"), Devotion (a taunt - "enemies can't attack your other Summons in its zone"; it absorbs nothing), Shadow Step and Shadow Cloak ("if active").
- **The rules codex** records those rulings, Petrified as an ordinary ailment that a cleanse removes, and ten stale passages fixed (Fogged against Guardians, Stealth against attacks, Leaping, Deep Infiltration, Seabound, the Avert count, spelling).

- **Wild Blessing and Safe Scouting can be cast again.** Neither accepted any target - not even yours - since they were added; a new test sweeps every targeted Spell for that gap.
- **The computer no longer stops playing when it has a Trap set.** The Energy it keeps back to spring the Trap was added to every price, a free Worker's included, so it could sit for turns with cards in hand; a free play is never held back now.
- **The computer listens to its own "no" for 32 Spells.** Their rules said not to cast them (The Final Dawn on a full board of its own, Forestry with no Nature Worker in the deck, Northern Lore from a deck of five...), and a general rule cast them anyway.
- **The computer casts Savage Pounce and Anticipation** (it planned them and never said X, so the cast was refused), Anticipation on the Summons its plan chose, and **Quick Reflexes** only when there is a discarded Lightning card to return.

- **The computer thinks about a third faster** on a crowded board: about 1.2 seconds less per turn on the late-game test board, with exactly the same decisions (80 whole turns on 38 boards replayed identically before and after).

- **Ilexa, Holly-Bound** prints one size larger; Rootcall sits a little lower to make room.
- **The designer's new art is in:** board backgrounds and borders, Empiros High Courts, Judgement Bell, Vanguard Paladin, Crosswind Lancer, Squallbreaker Glaive, Glemra and Stillfeather Quatl board pieces, Rocky Overhang, Jurian's deck picture.
- **A smaller game:** the documents and drafts in the project folder are no longer packed into it.

- **The match screen is about twice as fast to redraw.** On a crowded late-game board (twenty Workers, a dozen Summons, Runes, a Terrain) one redraw took 52-65 ms - more than three frames - every time anything happened; it now takes 29-32 ms. The stat reads under it are 2-3x faster (Attack 0.55 -> 0.28 ms, Defense/Magic/Resistance 1.25 -> 0.38 ms a Summon), which also speeds up the combat forecast and the computer's thinking (its threat read 0.6 -> 0.3 ms). Nothing plays or looks different: every change was checked old-against-new over hundreds of thousands of calls, and the board's screenshot is identical pixel for pixel.
- **Frames with a question window open or the combat forecast on** no longer search the whole board every frame.
- **A tool's test match can no longer overwrite your saved game** or `last_match.txt`.

- **Card faces are drawn without mipmaps** - the sharpest, as Chains of Devotion was before build 915. Builds 915 and 916 made every face softer; this undoes both, and every face now looks the way Chains did. Board pieces and tiles keep their mipmaps.

- **Three new pre-cons:** Chonzo's Calm, Jurian's Judgement and Ilsbet's Infected.
- **Card faces are sharp when shown small.** Build 915's mipmaps alone drew shrunk faces soft (Sol's Wings in the Deck Builder); the game now reads them one mipmap finer, which lands close to a proper downscale - smooth edges, crisp text.
- **Seven Light faces drawn in the engine from the designer's new art:** Elowen, Inquisitor Verren, Talas, Lum Knight Captain, Pearl of Life, To Oblivion and War Lion (whose Punishing is styled again).
- **Sol's Wings** prints "Treasure Spell - Enchantment - Light" - a Treasure Spell whose subtype is only in its Spell type no longer prints as a bare Treasure. Its old hand-made face is gone.
